name: Party

modes.label: Native product; see regime notes
modes.note: Incomplete or non-resource economics: rates remain null, never interpreted as free.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: Custom price; managed or self-hosted, local models through OpenCode, BAA support, 24/7 forward-deployed engineer.

caveats: Free one-time $100, 2 sessions/4 session-hours per day; Starter $20/month includes $20/month and $200 once, 10 sessions/20 session-hours per day; Pro $200 includes $400/month/$400 once and unlimited advertised session limits. Credit-to-compute exchange and machine shape unverified. Credits also fund agents/models; not all compute.
Monthly credits also pay model usage; platform has no published compute-only exchange, so plan allowances are not sufficient to price a workload.
Null values mean unknown, not free/unlimited. No model-token cost, tax or unverified ancillary charge included.
Native browser/device/task/credit prices with unknown CPU/RAM are deliberately non-priceable. Check regime before interpreting any partial resource estimate.

fleet.tiers: Free 2 sessions at once/4 session-hours per day; Starter 10/20; Pro unlimited advertised sessions/hours.
fleet.notes: Session limit separate from usage credits. 10 fits Starter; 50/300/1,000 notionally within Pro unlimited claim, not guaranteed resource/capacity allocation.

isolation.quote: Every agent session runs in an isolated sandbox with its own filesystem and process space. Sessions are isolated from one another
isolation.note: No hypervisor/VM is named; 'own filesystem and process space' phrasing without mention of a VM points to container-level isolation, not confirmed.

image_oci.quote: Environments define the runtime and boundaries for each session.
image_oci.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Party manages environments itself; no user-supplied Docker/OCI image option is documented.

nested_virt.quote: Party is the open, multiplayer workspace where your team and coordinated AI agents build together, from idea to merge.
nested_virt.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — a managed coding-agent workspace, not a VM/virtualization platform.

desktop.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — interaction is via chat threads and a live app Preview, not a VNC/RDP desktop.

own_agent_api.quote: Priya (Product Manager) asks Research... Engineer: I'll make invites optional...
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope as documented — Party's own agents (Product, Engineer, Auditor) are driven via chat/Flows in the app; no public API for driving them was found.

lang_python.quote: Product agent Codex, Engineer agent Claude Code, Auditor agent OpenCode
lang_python.note: Inferred: general-purpose coding harnesses (Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode) used to build software; no language restriction documented.

lang_node.quote: Product agent Codex, Engineer agent Claude Code, Auditor agent OpenCode
lang_node.note: Inferred: general-purpose coding harnesses build full-stack web apps (e.g. CRM, portals), implying Node/JS support; no restriction documented.

public_ipv4.quote: Try the live Preview and leave feedback as the change takes shape.

guest_firewall.quote: Every agent session runs in an isolated sandbox with its own filesystem and process space.
guest_firewall.note: derived: no root/full-VM access is documented for end users, so guest-side firewall configuration is not applicable.

secret_proxy.quote: Credentials are made available to sessions at runtime and are referenced by name in conversations and tooling. Our tooling is built to keep secret values out of transcripts, commits, and logs.
secret_proxy.note: Secrets are referenced by name and redacted from output, but this is not described as an HTTP-request-injecting proxy.
